generation_prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original square editorial illustration for a magazine cover about written city permission for temporary emergency cooling water at a proposed Texas data center. No typography. This is a sculptural metaphor, not an actual pipe network, signed document, engineering design or operating campus.

Make one exquisite hand-built clay systems model: a short horizontal milk-white porcelain pipe with a substantial valve body at its middle. Instead of a normal handle, a large cobalt fountain-pen nib is deliberately mounted upright on the valve spindle, as an unmistakable metaphor for written permission. The nib has a precise central slit and round breather hole but no engravings. At the right, the short pipe curves downward and ends above one cobalt ceramic water drop. Keep the construction simple, coherent and physically joined. No other pipes or valves.

Composition: central apparatus viewed from a gentle front three-quarter angle. On a 1080-square canvas all objects, including the nib and single drop, fit inside x=140..940 and y=230..690. These are hard framing bounds. Keep the entire top y=0..195 and bottom y=738..1080 empty cobalt field for later publication type. Do not crop any object. Full opaque square background.

Palette: saturated cobalt #254EDB, milk porcelain #F0F1E8, midnight #101D4C shadows, a trace of pale lime #DCE9A4 reflected light. Broad upper-left studio light, restrained soft shadow. Macro is the bold nib-and-valve silhouette; meso is the collar and flange; micro is glaze pooling and handworked ceramic edges. Elegant, tactile, visibly sculpted, no photoreal campus. Exclude text, numbers, logos, seals, maps, signatures, arrows, extra droplets, flags and decorative circuitry.

Edit the provided cobalt-background porcelain pen-valve illustration. Change only its framing and scale. Preserve the sculpture exactly: the cobalt fountain-pen nib as valve handle, ivory ceramic pipe and bolted flanges, single cobalt drop, glaze details, lighting and cobalt background. The previous subject is much too large for the cover. UNIFORMLY SHRINK the ENTIRE assembly including nib and drop to 60 percent of its current size, and move it so that on the 1080-square canvas every visible object fits between x235 and x845 and between y245 and y700. The nib tip must start below y245; the drop tip must end above y700. Leave a large uninterrupted cobalt field above and below. No added objects, no text, no labels, no outlines. Do not zoom in or fill the frame. Keep the same opaque square canvas. It should look like the same artwork viewed from farther away, centered horizontally in the middle band.

Edit this exact porcelain pen-valve illustration, preserving every material, join, nib, bolt, color and the single drop. Correct placement only. On the same square blue canvas, shift the WHOLE sculpture UPWARD by 85 pixels measured on a 1080px square. Also enlarge the whole sculpture uniformly by only 10 percent. All story objects must finish inside x240..840 and y220..695 on a 1080 canvas. The drop must be comfortably ABOVE the lower third of the canvas. Leave blue space below all objects for the cover headline, and above for the masthead. Do not add any object, text, number, mark or label. Keep opaque cobalt background and same gentle lighting. Do not crop the sculpture. This is a precise small upward placement correction, not a zoom-in to fill the canvas.

Keep this exact image unchanged in all respects EXCEPT move the complete porcelain pipe, pen nib, single drop and their shadows straight DOWN by 40 pixels measured on a 1080x1080 canvas (about 4 percent of canvas height). Do not resize, enlarge, shrink, rotate or redesign any object. Keep all horizontal positions exactly the same. Preserve the opaque blue background, glaze, lights and every detail. Extend the empty blue backdrop seamlessly where needed. The nib tip should be near y225 and the drop bottom near y715 on the 1080 canvas. No new objects, text, marks or labels. This is only a small downward translation to improve the upper margin for a magazine cover.
